fullPassage: Countershading is the process of optical flattening that provides camouflage to animals. When sunlight illuminates an object from above, the object will be brightest on top. The color of the object will gradually shade darker toward the bottom. This shading gives the object depth and allows the viewer to distinguish its shape. Thus even if an animal is exactly, but uniformly, the same color as the substrate, it will be easily visible when illuminated. Most animals, however, are darker above than they are below. When they are illuminated from above, the darker back is lightened and the lighter belly is shaded. The animal thus appears to be a single color and easily blends in with the substrate. This pattern of coloration, or countershading, reduces the visual impression of shape in the organism. It allows the animal to blend in with its background. What exactly does normal science involve? According to Thomas Kuhn it is primarily a matter of puzzle-solving. However successful a paradigm is, it will always encounter certain problems — phenomena which it cannot easily accommodate, or mismatches between the theory's predictions and the experimental facts. The job of the normal scientist is to try to eliminate these minor puzzles while making as few changes as possible to the paradigm. So normal science is a conservative activity — its practitioners are not trying to make any earth-shattering discoveries, but rather just to develop and extend the existing paradigm. In Kuhn's words, 'normal science does not aim at novelties of fact or theory, and when successful finds none'. Above all, Kuhn stressed that normal scientists are not trying to test the paradigm. On the contrary, they accept the paradigm unquestioningly, and conduct their research within the limits it sets. If a normal scientist gets an experimental result which conflicts with the paradigm, they will usually assume that their experimental technique is faulty, not that the paradigm is wrong. What is unusual about journalism as a profession is its lack of independence. In theory, practitioners in the classic professions, like medicine or the clergy, contain the means of production in their heads and hands, and therefore do not have to work for a company or an employer. They can draw their income directly from their clients or patients. Because the professionals hold knowledge, moreover, their clients are dependent on them. Journalists hold knowledge, but it is not theoretical in nature: one might argue that the public depends on journalists in the same way that patients depend on doctors, but in practice a journalist can serve the public usually only by working for a news organization, which can fire her or him at will. Journalists' income depends not on the public, but on the employing news organization, which often derives the large majority of its revenue from advertisers. In most of the world, capitalism and free markets are accepted today as constituting the best system for allocating economic resources and encouraging economic output. Nations have tried other systems, such as socialism and communism, but in many cases they have either switched wholesale to or adopted aspects of free markets. Despite the widespread acceptance of the free-market system, markets are rarely left entirely free. Government involvement takes many forms, ranging from the enactment and enforcement of laws and regulations to direct participation in the economy through entities like the U.S.'s mortgage agencies. Perhaps the most important form of government involvement, however, comes in the attempts of central banks and national treasuries to control and affect the ups and downs of economic cycles. One vivid example of how a market mindset can transform and undermine an institution is given by Dan Ariely in his book Predictably Irrational. He tells the story of a day care center in Israel that decided to fine parents who arrived late to pick up their children, in the hope that this would discourage them from doing so. In fact, the exact opposite happened. Before the imposition of fines, parents felt guilty about arriving late, and guilt was effective in ensuring that only a few did so. Once a fine was introduced, it seems that in the minds of the parents the entire scenario was changed from a social contract to a market one. Essentially, they were paying for the center to look after their children after hours. Some parents thought it worth the price, and the rate of late arrivals increased. Significantly, once the center abandoned the fines and went back to the previous arrangement, late arrivals remained at the high level they had reached during the period of the fines. The right to be forgotten is a right distinct from but related to a right to privacy. The right to privacy is, among other things, the right for information traditionally regarded as protected or personal not to be revealed. The right to be forgotten, in contrast, can be applied to information that has been in the public domain. The right to be forgotten broadly includes the right of an individual not to be forever defined by information from a specific point in time. One motivation for such a right is to allow individuals to move on with their lives and not be defined by a specific event or period in their lives. For example, it has long been recognized in some countries, such as the UK and France, that even past criminal convictions should eventually be "spent" and not continue to affect a person's life. Despite the reason for supporting the right to be forgotten, the right to be forgotten can sometimes come into conflict with other rights. For example, formal exceptions are sometimes made for security or public health reasons. There is no doubt that the length of some literary works is overwhelming. Reading or translating a work in class, hour after hour, week after week, can be such a boring experience that many students never want to open a foreign language book again. Extracts provide one type of solution. The advantages are obvious: reading a series of passages from different works produces more variety in the classroom, so that the teacher has a greater chance of avoiding monotony, while still giving learners a taste at least of an author's special flavour. On the other hand, a student who is only exposed to 'bite-sized chunks' will never have the satisfaction of knowing the overall pattern of a book, which is after all the satisfaction most of us seek when we read something in our own language. Moreover, there are some literary features that cannot be adequately illustrated by a short excerpt: the development of plot or character, for instance, with the gradual involvement of the reader that this implies; or the unfolding of a complex theme through the juxtaposition of contrasting views. There is a practice inspired by Yoda, the wise Jedi master from the Star Wars films, who represents ultimate wisdom, truth, and insight — all the answers we need in one entity. I believe the wisdom of Yoda is in every team but not in any one of us alone. Only by drawing out of everyone their point of view can we achieve the best, boldest answers. The problem is that most people don't have the courage to speak up. So, you're going to make Yoda the "safe word" for business. To begin, you can appoint a few Yodas in any meeting or group conversation, though it is particularly useful in potentially difficult or volatile situations. By giving the Yodas explicit permission to raise their hand and call a "Yoda moment," and say the hard things or act as a referee between competing perspectives, you are making it safe for others to do the same. Taking time to introduce the Yoda concept and to select some Yodas for the role goes a long way to diffusing tension in challenging conversations before it hinders frankness and ultimately your business results. Opportunities arise when supply and demand for products or services are not coordinated, that is when markets are not (as is often assumed) in natural states of equilibrium. Being off balance, the market needs a little help, and it is the entrepreneurial figure of action (rather than a regulator such as the state) who rises to the challenge, discovering opportunities when they come along. In Kirzner's view, entrepreneurs are alert to opportunities by discovering market errors, such as product or service shortages, and exploit these by acquiring resources at lower prices than they can later sell them for. Thus, the entrepreneur is at all times scanning the horizon, as it were, ready to make discoveries. By taking advantage of price differences, entrepreneurs help move the market towards equilibrium by serving unmet needs and correcting resource misallocations. One interesting aspect here is that the entrepreneur does not need to possess the means of production: they only need to recognise and act on opportunities profiting from unexploited gain ('arbitrage'), which means they are not just rational calculators but also risk-takers, which in turn justifies their profits. In the past, it was often assumed that competence acquired in the first language (L1) was qualitatively different from that in a second language (L2) or any subsequent language. This privileging of the "native language" led to many popular misconceptions, such as believing that children of bilingual parents would never fully acquire either language, remaining somehow linguistically disadvantaged. Such claims are due to the belief that monolingualism is the norm, and they are held by many in the United States and other countries where a single language is politically or socially dominant. That this view must be wrong can easily be seen from the fact that many people in the world are speaking more than one language. In fact, it is bilingualism or trilingualism rather than monolingualism that is most common. Even in supposedly monolingual nations like the United States, U.S. Census figures from 2014 showed that at least 20 percent of the population regularly spoke a language other than English, and 53 percent of these people also spoke English. From Descartes to the present, reason has been prized in Western culture, standing as the chief virtue of the modernist world-view. As we are led to believe, it is the power to reason that sets humans above the remainder of the animal kingdom, and is essential for human survival. Literary study suggests otherwise. Among the most important objections are those of the French literary theorist Jacques Derrida. Derrida's writings, often identified as deconstructionist, are ambiguous and open to many interpretations. From one perspective, however, they significantly undermine the cultural investment in human reason. Consider two major premises. First, suggests Derrida, rational arguments bring about a massive suppression of meaning. Broadly put, when we are convinced by a rational argument we do not know more, but less. Second, if closely examined, all rational arguments will collapse. Rationality, then, is not a foundation for anything — for our institutions of government and science, for example, or as a way of deciding on what is moral or worthwhile. Rather, Derrida suggests, our 'good reasons' are in the end both suppressive and empty. How the children learn new concepts? The traditional view of conceptual change was that new learned theories replace old ones: once a children learns that the Earth rotates around the sun, their previous theory (based on their experience of seeing the sun move) that the sun rotates around the Earth, would be overwritten. Recent evidence from adults suggests something more surprising: that these old, incorrect theories remain stored in the brain; often we still need them to drive our perceptual expectations such as where to look for the sun in the sky. But in an educational context, we need inhibitory control to suppress them in order to reach the newer, correct theories. The naive incorrect theory is more familiar and automatic; the new theory need time and deliberate suppression of the old theory to be actively retrieved. Copying is pedestrian. Copying is peculiar. On the one hand, copying makes us what we are. Our bodies take shape from the transcription of protein templates, our languages from the mimicry of privileged sounds, our crafts from the repetition of prototypes. Cultures hold together in the faithful transmission of rituals and rules of conduct. To copy cell for cell, word for word, image for image, is to make the known world our own. On the other hand, we are not identical, nor do we wish to think of ourselves as clones. Copying is ultimately imperfect, our errors eventually our heirs. The more widespread the act of copying, the greater the likelihood of significant mistranscription. Genetic slip or evolution, written mistake or midrash, miscopying raises hard questions about identity, security, and integrity. The same technical advances that make our skill at copying so impressive also intensify the dilemmas of forgery. We use copies to certify originals, originals to certify copies, then we stand confused. While discussions of human credulity often portray children as being highly credulous, experiments show that young children already use sophisticated methods for deciding whom to trust. In some such experiments, children interact with two individuals who give different names to previously unfamiliar objects. The child must decide whom to believe. In general, from an early age children would choose to believe a person they have a strong relationship with over a stranger. At age three, they would still do this even if the familiar person has a history of having given names to objects that the child recognized to be wrong. By age five, though, they will give more credence to a relative stranger who has some history of having been accurate than to a familiar person with a record of inaccuracy. What happens if there are two strangers to choose between with similar records of accuracy? Then the stranger who comes from the same cultural group as the child, as determined by accent, for example, is the one believed. Experiments have also been done on adults, who, like children, use information about the source of theories to decide whether to adopt them. We tend to follow opinion leaders, people in authority and those whose beliefs we share. Similar experiments show that among chimpanzees, those with higher status are trusted more. We all need ways of deciding whom to believe. Evolution has provided us and other species a start.

Thus even if an animal is exactly, but uniformly, the same color as the substrate, it will be easily visible when illuminated. Most animals, however, are darker above than they are below. When they are illuminated from above, the darker back is lightened and the lighter belly is shaded. The animal thus appears to be a single color and easily blends in with the substrate. This pattern of coloration, or countershading, __________ in the organism. It allows the animal to blend in with its background.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 역광 음영(countershading)은 생물의 형태에 대한 시각적 인상을 줄여 준다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① reduces the visual impression of shape(형태의 시각적 인상을 줄이다) — 등이 밝아지고 배가 어두워져 동물이 단색으로 보이며 배경에 섞인다는 앞 내용의 결론으로, 형태 인상을 '줄인다'가 정확히 부합 ← 정답.

❌ ② increases the brightness of the back(등의 밝기를 높이다) — 위에서 빛을 받을 때 어두운 등이 밝아지는 것은 부분 현상일 뿐, 이 문장이 말하는 전체 효과(형태 인상 감소)와 어긋난다.

❌ ③ reveals the exact outline of the body(몸의 정확한 윤곽을 드러내다) — 위장의 목적은 윤곽을 '감추는' 것이므로 정반대.

❌ ④ changes the animal's actual color(동물의 실제 색을 바꾸다) — 실제 색이 아니라 '단색으로 보이게' 하는 것이므로 부적절.
det.tip: appears to be a single color and blends in → reduces the visual impression of shape.

questions.passage: What exactly does normal science involve? According to Thomas Kuhn it is primarily a matter of puzzle-solving. However successful a paradigm is, it will always encounter certain problems — phenomena which it cannot easily accommodate, or mismatches between the theory's predictions and the experimental facts. The job of the normal scientist is to try to eliminate these minor puzzles while making as few changes as possible to the paradigm. So normal science is __________ — its practitioners are not trying to make any earth-shattering discoveries, but rather just to develop and extend the existing paradigm. In Kuhn's words, 'normal science does not aim at novelties of fact or theory, and when successful finds none'. Above all, Kuhn stressed that normal scientists are not trying to test the paradigm. On the contrary, they accept the paradigm unquestioningly, and conduct their research within the limits it sets. If a normal scientist gets an experimental result which conflicts with the paradigm, they will usually assume that their experimental technique is faulty, not that the paradigm is wrong.

det.korean: 정상 과학은 기존 패러다임을 유지·확장하려는 '보수적 활동'이다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① a revolutionary pursuit(혁명적 추구) — 「not trying to make any earth-shattering discoveries」와 정반대.

❌ ② an unpredictable gamble(예측 불가능한 도박) — 사소한 퍼즐을 풀며 패러다임 변화를 최소화한다는 안정성과 어긋난다.

❌ ③ a purely theoretical debate(순전히 이론적 논쟁) — 정상 과학자는 패러다임을 '검증'하지 않고 그 한계 안에서 연구한다.

✅ ④ a conservative activity(보수적 활동) — 대단한 발견을 노리지 않고 기존 패러다임을 발전·확장하며 의심 없이 받아들인다는 뒤 내용과 정확히 부합 ← 정답.

questions.passage: One vivid example of how a market mindset can transform and undermine an institution is given by Dan Ariely in his book Predictably Irrational. He tells the story of a day care center in Israel that decided to fine parents who arrived late to pick up their children, in the hope that this would discourage them from doing so. In fact, the exact opposite happened. Before the imposition of fines, parents felt guilty about arriving late, and guilt was effective in ensuring that only a few did so. Once a fine was introduced, it seems that in the minds of the parents the entire scenario was changed from a social contract to a market one. Essentially, they were paying for the center to look after their children after hours. Some parents thought it worth the price, and the rate of late arrivals increased. Significantly, once the center abandoned the fines and went back to the previous arrangement, late arrivals remained at the high level they had reached during the period of the fines.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.korean: 벌금 도입 후 지각 비율은 '증가'했다. ②는 이와 반대.
det.analysis:
❌ ① (어린이집은 부모의 지각을 막으려는 바람으로 벌금을 도입했다) — 「decided to fine parents who arrived late ..., in the hope that this would discourage them from doing so」와 일치.

✅ ② (벌금이 도입된 뒤 지각 비율이 줄었다) — 본문은 「the rate of late arrivals increased」라 하여 오히려 '늘었다'고 하므로 정반대 ← 정답.

❌ ③ (벌금 이전에는 죄책감이 지각을 적게 유지했다) — 「guilt was effective in ensuring that only a few did so」와 일치.

❌ ④ (벌금을 없앤 뒤에도 지각은 높은 수준으로 유지되었다) — 「late arrivals remained at the high level they had reached during the period of the fines」와 일치.
det.tip: the rate of late arrivals increased = 지각이 늘었다(벌금의 역효과).

ch: The day care center introduced fines hoping to discourage parents from picking up their children late.
After the fines were introduced, the rate of late arrivals decreased.
Before the fines, parents' guilt kept the number of late pickups low.

questions.passage: The right to be forgotten is a right distinct from but related to a right to privacy. The right to privacy is, among other things, the right for information traditionally regarded as protected or personal not to be revealed. The right to be forgotten, in contrast, can be applied to information that has been in the public domain. The right to be forgotten broadly includes the right of an individual not to be forever defined by information from a specific point in time. One motivation for such a right is to allow individuals to move on with their lives and not be defined by a specific event or period in their lives. For example, it has long been recognized in some countries, such as the UK and France, that even past criminal convictions should eventually be "spent" and not continue to affect a person's life. Despite the reason for supporting the right to be forgotten, the right to be forgotten can sometimes come into conflict with other rights. For example, formal exceptions are sometimes made for security or public health reasons.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.korean: 잊힐 권리는 이미 '공개된' 정보에도 적용된다. ③은 이와 반대.

❌ ① (잊힐 권리는 사생활 권리와 구별되지만 관련이 있다) — 「a right distinct from but related to a right to privacy」와 일치.

❌ ② (사생활 권리는 보호·개인 정보가 드러나지 않게 하는 것과 관련된다) — 「the right for information ... regarded as protected or personal not to be revealed」와 일치.

✅ ③ (잊힐 권리는 늘 비공개로 유지된 정보에만 적용된다) — 본문은 「can be applied to information that has been in the public domain」이라 하여 '공개된 정보'에도 적용된다고 하므로 정반대 ← 정답.

❌ ④ (영국·프랑스 같은 나라에서는 과거의 유죄 판결조차 결국 '소멸'될 수 있다) — 「even past criminal convictions should eventually be "spent"」와 일치.
det.tip: applied to information that has been in the public domain = 공개된 정보에도 적용.

questions.passage: Copying is pedestrian. Copying is peculiar. On the one hand, copying ①<u>make</u> us what we are. Our bodies take shape from the transcription of protein templates, our languages from the mimicry of privileged sounds, our crafts from the repetition of prototypes. Cultures hold together in the faithful transmission of rituals and rules of conduct. To copy cell for cell, word for word, image for image, is ②<u>to make</u> the known world our own. On the other hand, we are not identical, nor do we wish to think of ourselves as clones. Copying is ultimately imperfect, our errors eventually our heirs. The more widespread the act of copying, the greater the likelihood of significant mistranscription. Genetic slip or evolution, written mistake or midrash, miscopying ③<u>raises</u> hard questions about identity, security, and integrity. The same technical advances that make our skill at copying so impressive also ④<u>intensify</u> the dilemmas of forgery. We use copies to certify originals, originals to certify copies, then we stand confused.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ① make → makes: 동명사 주어 copying은 단수 취급하므로 단수동사 makes가 맞다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① make — 주어가 동명사 copying(단수 취급)이므로 makes가 되어야 한다(copying makes us what we are). 복수동사 make는 수 일치 위반 ← 정답.

❌ ② to make — 「To copy ... is to make the known world our own」에서 be동사의 보어로 쓰인 to부정사로 적절하다.

❌ ③ raises — 주어 miscopying(단수 동명사)에 맞춘 단수동사로 적절하다.

❌ ④ intensify — 주어 The same technical advances(복수)에 맞춘 복수동사로 적절하다. that make ...는 advances를 수식하는 관계절이다.
det.tip: 동명사 주어는 단수 취급: copying makes(O). 뒤의 miscopying raises(O)와 대조.

ch: ①
②

questions.passage: In most of the world, capitalism and free markets are accepted today as constituting the best system for allocating economic resources and encouraging economic output. Nations have tried other systems, such as socialism and communism, but in many cases they have either switched wholesale to or adopted aspects of free markets. Despite the widespread acceptance of the free-market system, markets are rarely left entirely free. Government involvement takes many forms, ranging from the enactment and enforcement of laws and regulations to direct participation in the economy through entities like the U.S.'s mortgage agencies. Perhaps the most important form of government involvement, however, comes in the attempts of central banks and national treasuries to control and affect the ups and downs of economic cycles.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 자유시장 체제가 널리 받아들여지지만 시장이 완전히 자유로운 경우는 드물고, 정부가 여러 형태로 개입한다는 내용.
det.analysis:
❌ ① how socialism and communism outperform free-market systems(사회주의와 공산주의가 자유시장 체제를 능가하는 방식) — 본문은 여러 나라가 다른 체제를 시도했지만 오히려 자유시장으로 '전환'했다고 하므로 정반대.

❌ ② the entrepreneur's role in discovering market imbalances(시장 불균형을 발견하는 기업가의 역할) — 이 글에서 다루지 않는 다른 소재.

❌ ③ why central banks should never interfere with economic cycles(중앙은행이 경제 순환에 결코 개입해선 안 되는 이유) — 본문은 중앙은행·국고의 개입을 '가장 중요한' 정부 개입 형태로 들므로 정반대.

✅ ④ the various forms of government involvement in free-market economies(자유시장 경제에서 이루어지는 정부 개입의 다양한 형태) — 시장이 완전히 자유로운 경우는 드물며 법의 제정·집행부터 중앙은행의 경기 조절까지 정부가 여러 형태로 개입한다는 글 전체의 핵심과 정확히 부합 ← 정답.

questions.passage: There is a practice inspired by Yoda, the wise Jedi master from the Star Wars films, who represents ultimate wisdom, truth, and insight — all the answers we need in one entity. I believe the wisdom of Yoda is in every team but not in any one of us alone. Only by drawing out of everyone their point of view can we achieve the best, boldest answers. The problem is that most people don't have the courage to speak up. So, you're going to make Yoda the "safe word" for business. To begin, you can appoint a few Yodas in any meeting or group conversation, though it is particularly useful in potentially difficult or volatile situations. By giving the Yodas explicit permission to raise their hand and call a "Yoda moment," and say the hard things or act as a referee between competing perspectives, __________. Taking time to introduce the Yoda concept and to select some Yodas for the role goes a long way to diffusing tension in challenging conversations before it hinders frankness and ultimately your business results.

questions.passage: Opportunities arise when supply and demand for products or services are not coordinated, that is when markets are not (as is often assumed) in natural states of equilibrium. Being off balance, the market needs a little help, and it is the entrepreneurial figure of action (rather than a regulator such as the state) who rises to the challenge, discovering opportunities when they come along. In Kirzner's view, entrepreneurs are alert to opportunities by discovering market errors, such as product or service shortages, and exploit these by acquiring resources at lower prices than they can later sell them for. Thus, the entrepreneur is at all times scanning the horizon, as it were, ready to make discoveries. By taking advantage of price differences, entrepreneurs help move the market towards equilibrium by serving unmet needs and correcting resource misallocations. One interesting aspect here is that the entrepreneur does not need to possess the means of production: they only need to recognise and act on opportunities profiting from unexploited gain ('arbitrage'), which means __________, which in turn justifies their profits.

det.korean: 'spent'는 과거의 유죄 판결이 결국 효력을 잃고 더는 그 사람의 삶에 영향을 주지 않게 됨을 뜻한다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① be fully paid off with a large sum of money(많은 돈으로 완전히 갚아지다) — 'spent'를 돈을 '쓰다'라는 문자적 의미로 오해한 것이다.

✅ ② eventually lose its power to define a person's life(결국 한 사람의 삶을 규정하는 힘을 잃다) — 밑줄 바로 뒤 'and not continue to affect a person's life(더는 그 사람의 삶에 영향을 주지 않는다)'로 이어지고, 특정 시점의 정보로 영원히 규정되지 않을 권리라는 글의 취지와 부합 ← 정답.

❌ ③ be recorded permanently in official documents(공식 문서에 영구히 기록되다) — 잊힐 권리(영원히 규정되지 않을 권리)와 정반대이다.

❌ ④ be made public for security reasons(보안상의 이유로 공개되다) — 뒤에 나오는 예외 조항과 뒤섞은 오답으로, 밑줄의 의미와 무관하다.
det.tip: even past criminal convictions should eventually be 'spent' and not continue to affect a person's life → 판결의 효력이 소멸함.

questions.passage: What exactly does normal science involve? According to Thomas Kuhn it is primarily a matter of puzzle-solving. However successful a paradigm is, it will always encounter certain problems — phenomena which it cannot easily accommodate, or mismatches between the theory's predictions and the experimental facts. The job of the normal scientist is to try to ①<u>eliminate</u> these minor puzzles while making as few changes as possible to the paradigm. So normal science is a ②<u>conservative</u> activity — its practitioners are not trying to make any earth-shattering discoveries, but rather just to develop and extend the existing paradigm. In Kuhn's words, 'normal science does not aim at novelties of fact or theory, and when successful finds none'. Above all, Kuhn stressed that normal scientists are not trying to test the paradigm. On the contrary, they ③<u>reject</u> the paradigm unquestioningly, and conduct their research within the limits it sets. If a normal scientist gets an experimental result which conflicts with the paradigm, they will usually assume that their experimental technique is ④<u>faulty</u>, not that the paradigm is wrong.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ③ reject → accept: 정상 과학자는 패러다임을 의심 없이 '받아들인다'는 맥락이므로 reject(거부하다)는 정반대로 부적절.
det.analysis:
❌ ① eliminate — 정상 과학자의 일은 사소한 퍼즐을 '제거하려(eliminate)' 애쓰는 것이므로 적절하다.

❌ ② conservative — 대단한 발견을 노리지 않고 기존 패러다임을 발전·확장한다는 점에서 정상 과학은 '보수적(conservative)' 활동이라는 맥락에 적절하다.

✅ ③ reject — 원문은 accept(받아들이다)이다. 앞 문장 '패러다임을 검증하려 하지 않는다'와 대조되어(On the contrary) 정상 과학자는 패러다임을 의심 없이 '받아들이고' 그 한계 안에서 연구한다는 흐름이어야 하므로, reject(거부하다)는 정반대로 부적절 ← 정답.

❌ ④ faulty — 결과가 패러다임과 충돌하면 패러다임이 아니라 자기 실험 기법이 '잘못됐다(faulty)'고 여긴다는 맥락에 적절하다.
det.tip: On the contrary, they accept the paradigm unquestioningly = 오히려 의심 없이 받아들인다. reject는 모순.

questions.passage: From Descartes to the present, reason has been prized in Western culture, standing as the chief virtue of the modernist world-view. As we are led to believe, it is the power to reason that sets humans above the remainder of the animal kingdom, and is essential for human survival. Literary study suggests otherwise. Among the most important objections are those of the French literary theorist Jacques Derrida. Derrida's writings, often identified as deconstructionist, are ambiguous and open to many interpretations. From one perspective, however, they significantly undermine the cultural investment in human reason. Consider two major premises. First, suggests Derrida, __________. Broadly put, when we are convinced by a rational argument we do not know more, but less. Second, if closely examined, all rational arguments will collapse. Rationality, then, is not a foundation for anything — for our institutions of government and science, for example, or as a way of deciding on what is moral or worthwhile. Rather, Derrida suggests, our 'good reasons' are in the end both suppressive and empty.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말 뜻에 맞도록 [조건]에 맞게 빈칸을 (영어로) 완성하시오.
뜻: 합리적 논증은 의미의 대규모 억압을 초래한다.
[조건] (1) massive, of, bring, rational, a, suppression, about, meaning, arguments 를 모두 사용할 것 (2) 정확히 9단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: 합리적 논증은 의미의 대규모 억압을 초래한다.
det.analysis:
정답: rational arguments bring about a massive suppression of meaning

구문 분석: 주어 rational arguments(복수) + 구동사 bring about(~을 초래하다) + 목적어 a massive suppression of meaning. bring about은 '(결과를) 야기하다'라는 뜻의 타동사구이며, of meaning이 suppression을 수식한다. 주어가 복수이므로 동사원형 bring이 쓰인다.
det.tip: bring about = 초래하다(구동사). a massive suppression of meaning = 의미의 대규모 억압.

questions.passage: What is unusual about journalism as a profession is its lack of independence. In theory, practitioners in the classic professions, like medicine or the clergy, ①<u>contain</u> the means of production in their heads and hands, and therefore do not have to work for a company or an employer. They can draw their income directly from their clients or patients. Because the professionals hold knowledge, moreover, their clients are dependent on them. Journalists hold knowledge, but it is not theoretical in nature: one might argue that the public depends on journalists in the same way that patients depend on doctors, but in practice a journalist can serve the public usually only by ②<u>working</u> for a news organization, ③<u>which</u> can fire her or him at will. Journalists' income depends not on the public, but on the employing news organization, which often ④<u>derive</u> the large majority of its revenue from advertisers.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ derive → derives: 관계사 which의 선행사가 the employing news organization(단수)이므로 단수동사 derives가 맞다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① contain — 주어가 practitioners(복수)이므로 복수동사 contain은 수 일치에 맞아 적절하다.

❌ ② working — 전치사 by의 목적어 자리이므로 동명사 working이 적절하다(by working = ~함으로써).

❌ ③ which — 뒤에 주어가 빠진 불완전한 절(can fire her or him)을 이끄는 주격 관계대명사로, 사물 선행사 a news organization을 받으므로 적절하다.

✅ ④ derive — 관계사 which의 선행사가 the employing news organization(단수)이므로 단수동사 derives가 되어야 한다. 삽입 부사 often에 속지 말 것. 복수동사 derive는 수 일치 위반 ← 정답.
det.tip: 선행사 the employing news organization(단수) → which ... derives. 삽입어구 often에 속지 말 것.
